question.text:
Consider the following two transactions and schedule $\text{S}$ (time goes from top to bottom).
$$\begin{array}{c|c}
\text { Transaction } \text{T}_0 & \text { Transaction } \text{T}_1 \\
\hline r_0[\text{A}] & \\
w_0[\text{A}] & \\
& r_1[\text{A}] \\
& r_1[\text{B}] \\
& c_1 \\
r_0[\text{B}] & \\
w_0[\text{B}] & \\
c_0 &
\end{array}$$

Which of the following is true?

  1. $\mathrm{S}$ is conflict serializable(CS) But not view serializable(VS).
  2. $\mathrm{S}$ is VS but not CS.
  3. S is both CS and VS
  4. $\mathrm{S}$ is neither CS, nor VS.

Here is a context-free grammar $\text{G}=(\{\text{S, A, B}\},\{0,1\}, \text{P, S})$, where $\text{P}$ is the set of productions:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{S} \rightarrow 0 \text{A} \mid 1 \text{B} \mid \epsilon \\
& \text{A} \rightarrow 1 \text{S} \mid 0 \text{AA} \\
& \text{B} \rightarrow 0 \text{S} \mid 1 \text{BB}
\end{aligned}
$$
Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. The languages generated by $\mathrm{G}$ is set of strings which have equal number of $0\text{'s}$ and $1\text{'s}.$
  2. If $\mathrm{A}$ is the start symbol then the language generated by $\mathrm{G}$ is set of strings with one more $1$ than $0.$
  3. If $\text{B}$ is the start symbol then the language generated by $\mathrm{G}$ is set strings with one more $0$ than $1.$
  4. String $1001, 101010$ are generated by $\text{G}.$

Which of the following is the Language accepted by this automata?

  1. Set of all strings ending with $a.$
  2. Set of strings with at least one $a$ and an even number of $b\text{'s}.$
  3. Set of strings with at least one $a$ and an even number of $b\text{'s}$ following the last $a.$
  4. Set of strings ending with $a$ and an even number of $b\text{'s}$ following the last $a.$

Here is a simple $\text{B}^+$ tree with a root and $4$ leaves.

Assume that each node has room for $3$ keys and $4$ pointers, and the ordering of keys is alphabetic. Also assume that when a node is split, and there is an odd number of pointers, the new node with the larger number of pointers is to the left of the other. Suppose that we insert a record with key '$e$' into this tree. Draw the new tree. Which of the following would be the list of non-null keys in some node of the resulting tree (i.e. Key Content of some node)?

  1. $k$
  2. $e f g$
  3. $f$
  4. $dhk$

Consider a relation $\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B})$ that contains $r$ tuples; assume $r>0$. Make no assumptions about keys $\&$ assume that the domain of all attributes is integers.
 
Consider the following queries:

  • $\text{Q1}:(\text{R }\bowtie \text{R}) \bowtie \text{R}$
  • $\text{Q2}:\sigma_{\text{A>B}} \text{R} \cup \sigma_{\text{A<B}} \text{R}$

For a relational algebra expression $\mathrm{Q}$, Let $\min (\mathrm{Q}), \max (\mathrm{Q})$ be the minimum and maximum number of tuples that could be in the result of the expression $\mathrm{Q}.$

Which of the following is/are correct?

  1. $\min (\mathrm{Q} 1)=0 ; \min (\mathrm{Q} 2)=0$
  2. $\min (\mathrm{Q} 1)=r ; \min (\mathrm{Q} 2)=0$
  3. $\max (\mathrm{Q} 1)=rrr ; \max (\mathrm{Q} 2)=r$
  4. $\max (\mathrm{Q} 1)=r ; \max (\mathrm{Q} 2)=r$

Let $\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b})$ be a schema and $\mathrm{Q} 1$ and $\mathrm{Q} 2$ are queries on $\mathrm{R}$.

Q1: SELECT * FROM R;
Q2: (SELECT * FROM R) INTERSECT (SELECT * FROM R);

Which of the following statements is true?

  1. $\text{Q1}$ and $\text{Q2}$ produce the same answer.
  2. The answer to $\text{Q1}$ is always contained in the answer to $\text{Q2}.$
  3. The answer to $\text{Q2}$ is always contained in the answer to $\text{Q1}.$
  4. $\text{Q1}$ and $\text{Q2}$ produce different answers.

Let $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ be two stations attempting to transmit on an Ethernet. Each has frames ready to send all the time; $\text{A's}$ frames will be numbered $\text{A1, A2}$, and so on, and $\text{B's}$ similarly. Let $\text{T}=51.2$ $\mu$ be the exponential backoff base unit. Suppose $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ simultaneously attempt to send frame $1,$ collide, and happen to choose backoff times of $0 \times \text{T}$ and $1 \times \text{T}$, respectively, meaning $\text{A}$ wins the race and transmits $\text{A} 1$ while Bwaits. At the end of this transmission, $\text{B}$ will attempt to retransmit $\text{B} 1$ while $\text{A}$ will attempt to transmit $\text{A} 2$. These attempts will collide, but now $\text{A}$ backs off for either $0 \times \mathrm{T}$ or $1 \times \mathrm{T}$, while $\text{B}$ backs off for time equal to one of $0 \times \mathrm{T}, \ldots, 3 \times \mathrm{T}$.

Give the probability that $\mathrm{A}$ wins this second backoff race after this collision; that is, $\text{A's}$ choice of backoff time is less than $\text{B's}.$

  1. $1/3$
  2. $5 / 8$
  3. $1 / 2$
  4. $3 / 8$

Which of the following regular expressions will not generate a string with two consecutive $1$s? (Note that $\varepsilon$ denotes the empty string.)

  1. $(1+\varepsilon)(01+0)^\ast$
  2. $(01+10)^ \ast$
  3. $(0+1) ^\ast(0+\varepsilon)$

  2. II only
  3. III only
  4. I and II only

Consider the paragraph $\text{Y} :$

Assume set $\text{A}$ is a subset of set $\text{B}.$ We know that if a property $\text{P}$ is satisfied by ALL elements of $\text{B}$ then it is also satisfied by ALL elements of $\text{A}$ since $\text{A}$ is a subset of $\text{B}$.

A student $\mathrm{X}$ has the following argument about closure properties of DCFL set :

We understand that the DCFL set(set of all DCFL languages) is not closed under Union. However, the DCFL set is a proper subset of the CFL set and the CFL set is closed under union. So how can a proper subset Not inherit the global properties of its parent set?

So, by paragraph $\text{Y},$ If the CFL set is closed under union then the DCFL set should also be closed under union since the DCFL set is a subset of the CFL set.

Where is the mistake in the above argument by student $\mathrm{X}?$ 

  1. There is no mistake in student $\text{X's}$ argument and the DCFL set is closed under union.
  2. The mistake is that the CFL set is not closed under union.
  3. The mistake is that from the said argument we can only deduce that union of two DCFL is CFL. We can't deduce that the union of two DCFL is DCFL.
  4. The mistake is that the set of DCFL is equal to the set of CFL.

It is known that the language $\text{L} \subseteq\{a, b\}^\ast$ that consists of all strings that contain an equal number of $a$ 's and $b$ 's is context-free. Let $\text{M}$ be the regular language $a \ast b^\ast .$

  3. $\text{L} \cap \text{M}=\left\{a^n b^m \mid n\right.$ is a positive integer less than integer $\left.m\right\}$.

  2. I only
  3. III only
  4. I and III

You want to transfer a file from Kanpur to Madras. For this problem, assume the following:

  • The size of file is $122,000$ bytes. It will be transferred in $1,500$-byte data packets, of which $40$ bytes are taken up with headers. The size of acknowledgment packets is $40$ bytes including header. Every packet is acknowledged.

  • The latency from Kanpur to Madras is $12 \mathrm{~ms}$, as is the latency in the opposite direction.

With Stop-and-Wait, how long will it take to transfer the file? (Include the time to receive the acknowledgment for the final data packet.)

  1. $2052.2 \mathrm{~ms}$
  2. $2108.8 \mathrm{~ms}$
  3. $1022.8 \mathrm{~ms}$
  4. $1091.02 \mathrm{~ms}$

  3. Lock upgrades are allowed during the shrinking phase of $\text{2PL}.$

Consider a database $\textsf{COMPANY}.$ The following two tables in this database store the data of employees and their dependents.
 
$\textsf{Employee (Fname, Lname}, \underline{\textsf{Ssn}}, \textsf{Sex, Dno)}$
$\textsf{Dependent} (\underline{\textsf{Essn, Dependent_name}}, \textsf{Sex, Relationship)}$

Now consider the following two SQL queries.
$\textsf{Q1:}$

SELECT E.Fname, E.Lname
FROM EMPLOYEE AS E
WHERE E.Ssn IN ( SELECT Essn
            FROM DEPENDENT AS D
            WHERE E.Fname=D.Dependent-name AND E.Sex=D.Sex );


$\textsf{Q2 :}$

SELECT E.Fname, E.Lname
FROM EMPLOYEE AS E, DEPENDENT AS D
WHERE E.Ssn=D.Essn AND E.Sex=D.Sex AND E.Fname=D.Dependent-name;


We want to Retrieve the name of each employee who has a dependent with the same first name and is the same sex as the employee.

Which of the following is true?

  1. $\textsf{Q1}$ produces the desired result, $\textsf{Q2}$ does not.
